Local source import analysis and compiler-derived lexical scope checks now reject forged-authorizer global rebinding, unbound-local fallbacks and missing parent package initializers. An additional output-framing leak is fixed: explicit framework envelopes replace payload-shape inference, final callbacks mediate complete application values, and interrupt contents participate in output label collection/redaction. A real-router baseline/current regression confirms the baseline publishes a synthetic secret field and the revised route redacts it. The resulting publication inventory has 58 entries, 10 verified and 48 unresolved; the expanded API surface remains part of the proof obligation. Legacy async event iterators v1/v2 now mediate inner-node event records and close producers on exit. The saved synthetic regression changes from two leaking events per version to zero; SGV109 detects the archived direct-return path. Other publication and callback APIs remain part of the open composition obligation. The subsequently observed inherited async log leak is also repaired: full log states are authorized, and only effective root-replacement patches/snapshots are published. Both log modes retain useful allowed output and suppress the saved canary; original leaking observations remain preserved. Direct callback handlers, state APIs and complete provenance/composition still require broader verification. Direct observer callbacks now pass through output mediation before handler delivery, with observer binding, effective-value reconstruction, approval continuations and cancellation handling. The prospective synthetic baseline leaked one callback record per sync/async case; after-final.json records zero. Stream taps receive effective values while computation retains original values. Error callbacks do not receive live tracebacks or approval capabilities. These bounded regressions do not discharge callback/state/derived-provenance composition; SGV901–903 remain open. Current-state and history APIs also had a prospective runtime leak: before.json records the canary in each current snapshot and two history rows per sync/async path. Complete snapshots now pass through the caller output boundary, including delegated subgraphs; replacement snapshots retain only effective content and omit original task/config/metadata fields. after.json records zero canary exposures. SGV110 detects eight archived raw-return/yield patterns and zero on the repaired source, without claiming helper or provenance proof. Source-admitted language programs now require structural type/effect derivations before execution; unsupported constructs and contract/type gaps refuse before effects. Runtime rechecks derivations and enforces declared inert terminal result types. This is conditional program evidence, with interpreter correspondence, terminal authorization and host composition still open; system completeness remains false. All 21 router entries now require a source-derived normal-return protocol: exact authorized-dispatch result or, on supported framework permission routes, the unchanged ESCALATE authorization record. Runtime admission rejects even source/bytecode-matched candidates that cannot prove that protocol. Pending approvals gain no publication authority; caller receiver binding and adapter/host composition remain open. The prospective source-only mutation capture is raw/router-return-proof/capture-v1/capture.json. Exact source-method receiver binding now requires an explicit type-identity guard and a checked fixed slot layout. HostRouter instances cannot shadow verified methods, and output publication captures its exact router through approval resume. The publication analysis now enters the actual router methods but still leaves policy/host slot authority and continuation publication unresolved. Bounded sync/async captures preserve useful approval output and refuse a substituted router before its methods execute; raw/receiver-binding-proof/capture-v1/capture.json retains source hashes and the open system claim. Native configuration/key, nested principal, and transform-argument shapes now refuse unknown Python protocols. Output receivers use fixed slots and matching router/host capture. Closed output-data admission repairs missing nested/message labels and mutable-approval subject binding; before/after synthetic probes and source bytes are saved under raw/output-data-admission. Current source proof exposes the reachable validator induction as unresolved; the earlier conditional branch proof is retained separately, not reused. The strict v2 report has zero implementation tasks and SGV901–903, with 2,940 declarations and 9/60 publication entries verified (51 unresolved). The replacement full-library run retains 4,496 passes and one source-proof assertion failure for the new decision argument helper. The assertion remains unchanged and is a concrete outstanding proof dependency; successful runtime mapping tests do not replace it. Final source archive raw/composition-proof/final-v2 matches all 229 inventory digests.

Runtime MAC now admits the exact dispatcher type on supported graph/ToolNode boundaries and still rejects forbidden work before native dispatch. A new cohort passes 20/20 operator-policy changes across fresh controllers (10 sync, 10 async): unchanged graph permit/manifest, optional private grant removed by the stricter deployment policy, useful required-input computation preserved, old container removed, and live policy replacement refused. Independent saved-evidence checks pass both cohorts. Unexpected cleanup backend exceptions now remain unconfirmed and quarantined. A production guardian now registers ownership before Docker creation and watches a controller-opened, transferred pidfd. The new v2 crash cohort passes 80/80 real SIGKILL trials (20 idle, 20 active-worker, 20 delayed-create-reply and 20 inherited-pipe cases), each after useful work. Saved-evidence verification confirms removal and guardian exit before harness cleanup, unchanged sources, receipts and the exact matrix. The first guardian cohort remains separate with its PID-lookup scope note. Guardian survival and daemon reachability remain required; simultaneous guardian/host failure and persistent daemon failure need external recovery. No complete lifecycle or composition proof is claimed. Historical evaluation-adapter pairs are unchanged.
